questions.q: Which four places does the lesson name as the real, concrete parts of the Trailblazer Community?
options: Feed, Groups, Topics, and Group Meetings
Badges, Points, Ranks, and Superbadges
Resumes, Portfolios, GitHub, and LinkedIn
Administrator, Developer, Consultant, and Architect
questions.explain: The lesson names Feed, Groups, Topics, and Group Meetings as the concrete places where community participation happens.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does a Platform App Builder add on top of Administrator skills?
options: Programmatic extension using Apex
The ability to design and deploy full custom applications declaratively, without code
Negotiating contracts with Salesforce directly
Designing org-wide architecture across multiple clouds
questions.explain: The lesson defines Platform App Builder as extending Administrator skills into full custom applications built declaratively, no code required.

questions.q: What is the current Salesforce CLI command, as confirmed in this lesson?
options: sfdx, the long-standing command that has never changed
salesforce-cli, a command that has never existed
force, the original 2010s-era command
sf, the current CLI shipped as the npm package @salesforce/cli -- sfdx was the previous major version
questions.explain: The lesson confirms the current CLI commands start with sf (package @salesforce/cli), with sfdx being the retired previous major version.

questions.q: What does setting a Trailhead profile to Public actually make visible to others?
options: Your certifications, community activity, badges, points, avatar, and about-me information
Nothing -- Public only affects search engine indexing
Your private login credentials
Only your name, with no other details
questions.explain: The lesson states a Public profile shows certifications, community activity, badges, points, avatar, and about-me information to anyone with the link.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against numbers that don't match between a resume and a portfolio page?
options: Because a careful reviewer will notice the mismatch and it damages credibility
Because applicant tracking systems reject resumes with any numbers at all
Because resumes should never include numbers
Because portfolios are not supposed to include any of the same deliverables as a resume
questions.explain: The lesson lists inconsistent numbers across documents as a common mistake, since it is the first thing a careful reviewer will notice.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say Salesforce certifications are meant to be taken in a sequence rather than any order?
options: Because Trailhead technically blocks you from registering out of order
Because certifications expire if taken out of order
Because each credential assumes the skills of the ones that typically come before it
Because only one certification can be active at a time
questions.explain: The lesson explains that each credential builds on assumed skills from earlier credentials in the sequence.

questions.q: What does the lesson say Salesforce Certified Platform Developer assesses?
options: Only declarative point-and-click configuration
Marketing Cloud subscriber data management
Tableau dashboard design
Developing and deploying custom business logic and interfaces using Apex and Visualforce
questions.explain: The lesson describes Platform Developer as assessing Apex and Visualforce skill for extending the Lightning Platform programmatically.

questions.q: What does the lesson say your LTV Customer Management System capstone already gives you toward exam preparation?
options: Nothing -- the capstone is unrelated to certification content
Only a resume bullet, with no exam value
A meaningful head start, since it already covers objects and fields, security, data management, and reports and dashboards
Full exam-equivalent certification on its own
questions.explain: The lesson states the capstone already covers a meaningful share of the Administrator exam's real territory.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does LTV Academy actually do with respect to Salesforce certifications?
options: It issues official Salesforce certifications directly to students who complete this course
It guarantees a passing score on any Salesforce exam
It prepares students for the skills and objectives behind the credentials, but does not issue certifications -- Salesforce does, through its own exam
It has no relationship to Salesforce certifications at all
questions.explain: The lesson states plainly that LTV Academy prepares students for the underlying skills and objectives but does not issue certifications itself.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend explaining your design while you draw rather than only after it's finished?
options: Because silence while drawing reads as uncertainty even when the candidate is confident
Because talking while drawing is required by Salesforce certification rules
Because the panel cannot hear you otherwise
Because drawing and talking at the same time is impossible, so it must be sequenced
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states that explaining as you draw prevents silence from being read as uncertainty.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend doing with the LTV Customer Management System capstone when answering interview questions?
options: Use it as a source of specific, real examples -- a migration decision, a security choice, a growth story, a pushback story
Avoid mentioning it since it's just a class project
Memorize its code structure verbatim and recite it regardless of the question
Only mention it if directly asked about coursework
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly recommends pulling specific, real examples from the capstone rather than giving generic answers.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say simply telling a client "that's against best practice" is a weaker answer than explaining the tradeoff?
options: Because it reads as rigid rather than expert, compared to explaining the downside in terms the client cares about and offering an alternative
Because best practices don't actually matter in consulting
Because clients are never allowed to hear the phrase "best practice"
Because it's technically inaccurate in every case
questions.explain: The lesson explains that translating the tradeoff into client-relevant terms and offering an alternative demonstrates expertise, while a bare rejection does not.

questions.q: In the fictional "Cascadia Outdoor Supply" scenario, what is the lesson's point about the phrase "a single view of the customer"?
options: It always means building a new mobile app
It is a real, verified customer named in Salesforce's own case studies
It has no bearing on the architecture at all
It's ambiguous -- it could mean a reporting/analytics need or an actual operational merge of orgs, and a strong answer asks which before proposing a design
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly labels the scenario as fictional and highlights that the phrase is ambiguous, requiring a clarifying question before any design proposal.

questions.q: What does the lesson say is the main layer a Developer interview adds on top of what an Administrator interview covers?
options: A credit check
A physical fitness test
Nothing -- the two interviews are identical
Code -- a live coding exercise, a take-home, or a code-review exercise
questions.explain: The lesson states Developer interviews add code-focused exercises on top of the same behavioral questions every role gets.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is "what would you do differently?" actually asking about?
options: Whether you regret taking the course
Whether you want to withdraw your application
Nothing specific -- it's just small talk
Scale and hindsight -- what the design assumed and what would strain at a larger size
questions.explain: The lesson frames this question as being about scale and hindsight, not a request for a confession of a mistake.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the actual goal of the small tasks taken on during days 30-60?
options: Building trust by listening to real pain points and fixing something real without breaking anything else
Proving you can rebuild the entire org alone
Avoiding any contact with existing tickets
Immediately proposing a full re-architecture
questions.explain: The lesson states the goal in this window is building trust through small, real fixes, not proving broad rebuilding ability.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe CTA as a "destination" rather than something a course alone can deliver?
options: Because CTA has been discontinued by Salesforce
Because CTA is only available to Salesforce employees
Because it additionally requires judgment built from real production experience over real years on the job, not just completed coursework
Because the credential no longer exists in any form
questions.explain: The lesson explains that CTA requires real-world architectural judgment, which a curriculum alone cannot substitute for.

questions.q: What fictional company does the lesson use as the concrete example for the LTV Customer Management System capstone?
options: Northbridge Insurance Group
Fairmont Logistics
Cascadia Outdoor Supply
Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co.
questions.explain: The lesson references Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co., the fictional company used in the LTV Customer Management System capstone course.
